pr.title: Do not unify borrowed locals in CopyProp.
pr.description:
Instead of trying yet another scheme to unify borrowed locals in CopyProp, let's just stop trying. We had already enough miscompilations because of this.

I'm convinced it's possible to have both unification of some borrowed locals and soundness, but I don't have a simple and convincing formulation yet.

Fixes https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/143491

pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions processed by CopyProp where a local is assigned a copy of another local and at least one of the two locals has its address taken (is in `borrowed_classes`), especially when the borrowed local can be mutated through that reference (or otherwise overwritten) after the copy and before the copied value is read again. Includes arguments that are borrowed (`fn borrowed<T>(x) { let a = x; ... &x ... }`) and locals borrowed after being copied (`_4 = _5; ... &_5; ... use(_4)`), including loop-carried cases where the borrow target changes each iteration.
analysis.summary: Confirmed bug-fix PR for CopyProp: the guard against unifying borrowed locals only rejected unification when BOTH locals were borrowed (`&&`); the fix rejects unification when EITHER is borrowed (`||`). Merging a borrowed local with a non-borrowed one was unsound because the borrowed local may be written through its reference before the copied value is read again, producing miscompilations (issue #143491). Regression tests pin the conservative behavior by keeping the copy assignments that were previously eliminated.
analysis.trigger: CopyProp considers unifying `local` with `head = copies[rhs]` and at least one of them is address-taken (`borrowed_classes.contains(local) || borrowed_classes.contains(head)`), while the other is not borrowed. Under the old `&&` guard this case was allowed and the copy was propagated/eliminated. A later write through the borrow to the borrowed local (for example via a loop-carried reference) then makes the propagated read stale, yielding incorrect behavior.
preconditions: Function is optimized by CopyProp (mir-opt pipeline runs SSA-based copy propagation).
A copy assignment connects two locals, forming a potential copy class.
Exactly one side of that copy has its address taken / is marked borrowed; the old guard required both to be borrowed to skip unification.
The borrowed local can be mutated through its reference (or else overwritten) after the copy and before the propagated value is read again, or the aliasing is otherwise not modeled.
pitfalls: Do not conflate the two independent conditions: 'borrow exists' and 'post-copy overwrite'. The guard is about forbidding unification of borrowed locals at all; the unsoundness is exposed when a write through the borrow intervenes before the next read.
The old guard's bug is specifically `&&` vs `||`; a correct check must trigger when EITHER side is borrowed, not only when both are.
Test-expectation hunks that remove `_x = copy _y` lines are evidence of the old (incorrect) propagation; retaining the copy line is the corrected output, not a failure to optimize.
A retained test name or old comment does not establish that a replacement pass is incorrect; compare actual value assignments in the decoded revisions.
This PR removes/blocks an optimization for soundness; do not describe it as introducing a new rewrite. It is conservative in the presence of borrowed locals because there is no aliasing model yet.
analysis.testStrategy: Add MIR-opt `copy-prop` regression tests using `// EMIT_MIR ...CopyProp.diff` and CHECK directives. (1) Borrow source after copy: `fn borrowed<T: Copy + Freeze>(x: T) -> bool { let a = x; opaque(&x); opaque::<T>(a) }`; CHECK that `_2 = copy _1` is retained and later call uses `copy _2`, not `copy _1`. (2) Borrow after copy: in a `mir!` block, `_4 = _5; *_1 = *_6; _6 = &_5; dump_var(_4)`; CHECK-NEXT that `_4 = copy _5` stays and the call reads `_4`. (3) Loop-carried aliasing regression `borrow_in_loop`: `let mut c; let mut p = &false; loop { let a = !*p; let b = !*p; c = a; p = &c; if a != b { return; } }`; CHECK that `a`, `b`, `c` remain distinct and that `&c` occurs without `&a`/`&b`, and that `a` and `b` values are used rather than unified. Run under both panic-abort and panic-unwind MIR dumps. Verify resulting diff shows copy statements preserved and uses still referencing the original locals.
evidence: Do not unify borrowed locals in CopyProp.
Instead of trying yet another scheme to unify borrowed locals in CopyProp, let's just stop trying. We had already enough miscompilations because of this.
-        // Do not unify two borrowed locals.
We must not unify a borrowed local with another that may be written-to before the borrow is
As we have no aliasing model yet, this means forbidding unifying borrowed locals.
